title: NBA Source: Kuminga Could Send Timberwolves to the Finals
htmlContent:
The NBA offseason has stretched on for nearly two months, yet the intrigue surrounding restricted free agent Jonathan Kuminga has only intensified. One NBA source recently painted a bold picture of what could happen if the former Golden State Warriors forward lands with the Minnesota Timberwolves this summer.

"Jonathan Kuminga, if he signs a one-year deal with Minnesota, somebody can probably pay him more money, but if he signs with the Timberwolves, let me tell you what's going to happen. Minnesota is going to the NBA Finals with Jonathan Kuminga, especially if you add him alongside Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball," the source told LandonBuford.com.

"And I'm telling you right now, Anthony Edwards is without question the best basketball player in the NBA, and you're going to see it. This team will go to the NBA Finals. And if the Timberwolves don't give Jonathan Kuminga big-time money, somebody is going to pay this kid huge money next offseason, because that combination is going to be dynamic."

It is a striking prediction for a Timberwolves team that has already made noise this offseason, but it underscores just how much buzz has followed Kuminga throughout free agency. The 23-year-old was one of the most sought-after names on the market, with several contenders viewing him as the missing piece to a championship puzzle.

For much of the summer, the Los Angeles Lakers appeared to be the frontrunner in the Kuminga sweepstakes. Reports indicated mutual interest between the two sides, with Los Angeles working behind the scenes to lock down his commitment as a new wing addition. The Cleveland Cavaliersalso entered the conversation, giving Kuminga a genuine three-team market to weigh as he considered his next chapter.

Minnesota's entry into the race came later, but it was no less significant. After missing out on a pursuit ofLeBron James, the Timberwolves shifted their attention to Kuminga, who could fill their vacant starting power forward spot. League sources indicated Minnesota was prepared to use its $6.06 million taxpayer mid-level exception to make a serious push for the young forward, according to HoopsHype's Michael Scotto.

The timing lines up. Minnesota parted ways with both Julius Randle and Naz Reid this summer, leaving a clear void in the frontcourt rotation. Kuminga's blend of athleticism, size, and scoring upside would address that need immediately, while also giving the Timberwolves a younger, more explosive frontcourt option than they have had in recent seasons.

Beyond the roster fit, the pairing with Anthony Edwards is what has scouts and analysts most intrigued. Edwards has established himself as one of the most dynamic scorers and closers in the league, and adding a high-flying, versatile forward like Kuminga could give Minnesota one of the most electric young duos in the Western Conference. Throw in the offseason addition of LaMelo Ball, acquired via trade, and the Timberwolves suddenly have a young core capable of trading buckets with anyone in the league.

Money will still play a major role in where Kuminga ultimately signs. He played last season on a one-year, $46 million contract, and his next deal figures to reflect the growth he has shown as a scorer and playmaker. If Minnesota is unwilling or unable to offer a long-term commitment at that price point, Kuminga could still choose a short-term deal with the Timberwolves in hopes of hitting an even bigger payday next offseason, just as the source suggested.

That scenario would be a calculated gamble for both sides. For Kuminga, it means betting on himself and his fit next to Edwards and Ball to boost his market value. For Minnesota, it means a short runway to prove the fit works before other suitors circle back with max-level offers.

Whether or not Minnesota ends up making a Finals run, as the source predicted, the fit on paper is undeniable. Edwards has already proven he can carry a team deep into the postseason, and pairing him with a rising talent like Kuminga, alongside a dynamic playmaker in Ball, would give the Timberwolves one of the most talented young trios in basketball.

For now, the basketball world waits to see where Kuminga lands. But if this NBA source is right, Minnesota may be building something special, and Jonathan Kuminga could be the final piece that turns the Timberwolves into legitimate title contenders.
